## Claims
- [source-backed] The two Theorem 5.4 families have \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators, with \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6, lines 14-42]
- [source-backed] The paper’s reported computation covers only \(r\le4,\ q=n-r\le5\). [source-6, lines 46-54]
- [proved] For \((r,q,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\), \(a=3\), \(b=2\), hence \(N=\binom53=10\). The two specialized families are
  \[
  F_1=(22,32,33,42,43,52,44,53,54,55),
  \]
  \[
  F_2=(22,221,2211,222,22111,2221,22211,2222,22221,22222).
  \]
- [computed] The truncated Pieri presentation has \(431\) Schur-basis columns and \(2130\) Pieri rows. Complementary-column eliminations for both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) use only unit pivots and leave no residual relation; the computed quotient is \(\mathbb Z^{10}\), with either family giving a basis. [artifact 0b05e147fd3b8f028a0683ee0de19704b04f214954cc0d8c387547f8371d7299]
- [proved] Assuming the standard identification \(A_+J_v=\sum_{k=1}^{6}h_kJ_v\) and that these two families generate \(J_v\), the computation implies both families are irredundant generators of \(J_v\), by graded Nakayama.

## Strategy
Use the Pieri presentation for \(J_v/A_+J_v\) in the first case beyond both reported bounds, \((r,q,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\), and certify freeness by unit-pivot elimination relative to each proposed family.

## Gaps
- The computation is finite and does not establish a uniform result.
- No separately implemented independent LR/Pieri or Smith-form verification was supplied; the elimination certificate requires independent audit.

## Next
Independently reproduce this \((5,6,2,2)\) certificate, preferably with direct LR relations and exact Smith normal form.
